title: Better than 90% of bodybuilding routines: 4 HORSEMEN by Brian Alsruhe
summary: NH reviews strongman Brian Alsruhe's 4 Horsemen giant-set program, praising its self-regulation, compact sessions and how it teaches lifters to program. For hypertrophy he would drop the four-week intensity waves and conditioning slot, add isolation work, avoid supersetting the main strength lift, and expand it into an 'eight horsemen' with two giant sets.
claims: Alsruhe gives the template away free and charges only to write programs for people, which encourages lifters to program for themselves; NH respects that and will not post the paid program
4 Horsemen, written by a strongman, is one of the best hypertrophy programs he has reviewed, clearly refined through real testing, unlike most bodybuilder and powerlifter programs
The giant-set format compresses sessions to 60-70 minutes, so four sessions a week take about four hours, yet the work is demanding
Blocks and four-week waves make sense for strength but are unnecessary for hypertrophy, though changing intensity and volume is still important for bodybuilders
Self-regulated programs that allow improvising tend to be the best-designed, because they need built-in mechanisms that make it possible
A good program makes you bigger and also teaches you to program while you run it
Giant sets with 90 seconds of rest between rounds are valid; he gives more rest and eases people in, and lifters who switch to giant sets rarely go back
The day is structured as A antagonist, B main mover (chosen first), C core and D conditioning, done as one giant set
Pairing each main lift with its antagonist is not as necessary for preventing imbalances as people think; benching one day and rowing another works too
He does not superset strength work, but Alsruhe pairs the main lift with the antagonist because of strongman conditioning needs and because his days have so few exercises
Superset core work every day so you actually do it; people who say squats and deadlifts alone give a six-pack tend to have guts
Alsruhe isolates the core but relies on compounds for arms and traps, which limits bodybuilders; if you isolate the core, isolate those muscles too
For hypertrophy, replace the conditioning slot with isolation work
On lower days Alsruhe uses an explosive antagonist like kettlebell swings rather than an RDL before squats, which is smart because lower-body muscles work together and fatigue each other
In his version the main mover comes first and the antagonist goes in a separate set, the core superset stays, and isolation replaces conditioning
His eight horsemen version uses two giant sets per day instead of one, with a minimalist option that keeps the original four slots
Alsruhe's intensity categories are light 60-70%, medium 65-75%, heavy 70-80% and brutal 75-85%, arranged in waves so two lifts are never brutal the same week
Short sessions with the main lift at 65% waste the steady tonnage bodybuilders need; evolving rep ranges control intensity without light, medium and heavy days
He programs ranges like 6-10 near AMRAP and expects about 8-9; once you regularly hit 10, add weight
Capping yourself at 70% when you could go higher is planning for future strength performance and suits strength athletes, not bodybuilders
He can do snatch-grip deadlifts for 8 reps to failure and squat to failure two days later because his body and recovery are adapted to frequent PRs
Strength-building ramp-up periods and assistance work at about 40% are not needed for bodybuilding and should be replaced with isolation and more work
Beginners will find this kind of giant set too hard on the cardiovascular system
Varying range of motion within the line of specificity, with partials and deficits, is smart and something good strength coaches understand
In his programs load never comes down; only tonnage rises week to week, and intensity and volume are managed within each session through evolving rep ranges
Hypertrophy 4 Horsemen day 1: DB or barbell rows 3-4x6-12, dips or bench 3-4x4-8, dragonflies 3-4xAMRAP, DB or EZ curls 3-4x6-10
Day 2: squats 3-4x4-8 first, then RDLs 3-4x6-12, hanging leg raises 3-4xAMRAP, shrugs or farmer's carries 3-4x10-15
Day 3: weighted chin-ups or pull-ups 3-4x4-6, DB or barbell OHP 3-4x6-10, hanging knee raises 3-4xAMRAP, skull crushers or French press 3-4x6-12
Day 4: deadlifts 1-3x2-5 first, then hack squats 3-4x10-15, Russian twists 3-4xAMRAP, seal or DB rows 3-4x6-10
exercises: does not tire the legs before squats the way an RDL would
quad work after the heavy hinge
upper back work without lower back load
